svg.title: Conquering Dirty Water: Dr John Snow’s Soho Pump & Bazalgette’s London Sewers (1854–1875)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 7 two-panel historical GIS map: the left panel shows Victorian London, the tidal River Thames, Westminster during the 1858 Great Stink, and Sir Joseph Bazalgette’s Northern and Southern High- and Low-Level Intercepting Sewers flowing east to Abbey Mills and Crossness pumping stations; the right panel zooms into Dr John Snow’s August–September 1854 Soho street grid (Oxford Street, Regent Street, Broad Street, Wardour Street, Dean Street) showing red cholera death clusters around the Broad Street Pump, the leaking cesspool at 40 Broad Street, and safe green zones at the Lion Brewery and Poland Street Workhouse.

text.tspan: Brick tunnels & steam pumps end cholera; 1875 clean-water law
Sewage-choked River Thames forces MPs to fund London sewers

g.text: ZOOM: DR JOHN SNOW’S SOHO INVESTIGATION (AUG–SEPT 1854)
KEY B — DR JOHN SNOW’S SOHO SPOT MAP (1854)
Cholera Deaths Clustered Around Broad St Pump (500+)
40 Broad Street Leaking Cesspool (3 ft from Pump Well)

text.tspan: 2. 40 Broad St Cesspool vs Lion Brewery (1854)
Leaking cesspool poisons well; beer-drinking workers survive!
Dr John Snow maps 500+ cholera deaths around one street pump

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 7 ENQUIRY: WATER, SANITATION & PUBLIC HEALTH
Conquering Dirty Water: Snow’s Soho Pump & Bazalgette’s Sewers (1854–75)
In 1854, Dr John Snow mapped Soho’s cholera deaths to one sewage-poisoned street pump—disproving “bad air” (miasma).
After the 1858 Great Stink, Bazalgette’s giant brick sewers and the compulsory 1875 Public Health Act cleaned up British towns.
